newsitem.title: USA: IPO SPOTLIGHT-MagiNet boosts shares, looks firm.
newsitem.headline: IPO SPOTLIGHT-MagiNet boosts shares, looks firm.

text.p: With demand looking strong for its market debut, MagiNet Corp has increased the number of shares to be offered in its upcoming initial public offering.
MagiNet supplies pay-per-view entertainment and interactive video services, like express checkout and room service, to the hospitality industry outside North America.

The Sunnyvale, California plans to begin offering in-room casino-style gaming, advertising, video games, financial news, Internet access and in-room shopping in certain markets beginning in 1997, it said in the filing.

About 5.5 million shares will be offered, up from 5.0 million, according to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. They are estimated to price between $12 to $14 each and will trade on the Nasdaq under the proposed symbol "MGNT". That makes the IPO worth roughly $71.5 million.

Several IPO analysts have said early demand for shares looks strong, although MagiNet has yet to post a profit since it began installing its systems in 1993. Its revenues were $8.7 million in for the year ended December 31, 1995.
At June 30, 1996 MagiNet served 138 hotels with 49,683 rooms, with an additional 20,868 rooms in backlog.

So far, MagiNet has focused on hotels in the Pacific Rim such as Thailand, Australia, Japan, Hong Kong and other areas. In the filing, it said it plans to expand further in the region and move into Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
Its competitors include SpectraVision Inc, which has been uperating in bankruptcy since June 1995 and was purchased by Ascent Entertainment Group.
Another rival, LodgeNet Entertainment Corp has never posted a profit. Lodgenet operates mostly in the United States, but has recently said it plans to enter some of MagniNet's markets.

About 4.4 million shares will be offered in the United States and Canada and 1.1 million will be offered globally. The deal is tentatively scheduled for early December, according to lead underwriter Lehman Brothers.
